# Introduction

The following document is the specification of the REST API for Sales management. It includes the model definition as well as all available operations.

This API provides interfaces for Sales Lead, Sales Opportunity and the other management capabilities to support the sales activities to build relationship with the prospect customer who could be a person or organization that has an interest in the goods and/or services and possibly become the actual customers with one or more subscriptions.

The Lead corresponds to the nominal result of an interaction involving a prospective customer towards one of offers or services. It is the first stage (S) of the SPANCO process (a six-stage sales methodology originally developed by Rank Xerox to help sales teams convert leads into loyal customers, including: Suspect, Prospect, Analysis, Negotiation, Closure and Order).

A prospect could have expressed a commercial interest or a commercial interest has been detected from his behavior analysis. The Lead Management function enables to collect, evaluate and attribute the leads to the appropriate sales representatives.

The lead is an interest concerning an offer family or a product line, or expressed literally during an interaction, possibly further to a marketing campaign, and it must be handled and specified to become an opportunity or an order.

In a nominal way, once the interest towards offers or services is confirmed and the prospective customer clearly identified, then along with the customer, an Opportunity is created.

In some cases, for example e-commerce or B2C scenarios, a SalesLead can directly relate to an Order.

# SAMPLE USE CASES

Reader will find example of use cases using Open APIs in “IG1228 How to use ODA – Using Open APIs to realize Use Cases” document.

Use case 1: A prospect shows interest in a commercial link

![](data:image/png;base64,)

Use case 2: A prospect asks for information in a trade show

![](data:image/png;base64,)

Use case 3: A prospect is the target of a marketing mailing campaign

![](data:image/png;base64,)

![](data:image/png;base64,)

Use Case 4: A prospect customer is interested in your products. As a Sales Person, you are planning to now meet the customer and understand their requirements, analyze them, perform lead qualification and based on that, tries to present a solution from their offerings. An opportunity is created if the prospect customer is a B2B customer. In cases where the customer is a B2C customer, a product order can be generated based on the interest from the customer

![](data:image/png;base64,)

Use Case 5: An existing customer is interested in the some of the other products that your company offers. As a Sales Person, you are planning to now meet the customer and understand their requirements, analyze them and based on that, tries to present a solution from their offerings. As the customer already exists, a new opportunity can be created.

![](data:image/png;base64,)

# Support of polymorphism and extension patterns

Support of polymorphic collections and types and schema based extension is provided by means of a list of generic meta-attributes that we describe below. Polymorphism in collections occurs when entities inherit from base entities, for instance a BillingAccount and SettlementAccount inheriting properties from the abstract Account entity.

Generic support of polymorphism and pattern extensions is described in the TMF API Guidelines, Part 2 (TMF630).

The @type attribute provides a way to represent the actual class type of an entity. For example, within a list of Account instances some may be instances of BillingAccount where other could be instances of SettlementAccount. The @type gives this information. All resources and sub-resources of this API have a @type attributes that can be provided when this is useful.

The @referredType can be used within reference entities (like for instance an AccountRef object) to explicitly denote the actual entity type of the referred class. Notice that in reference entities the @type, when used, denotes the class type of the reference itself, such as BillingAccountRef or SettlementAccountRef, and not the class type of the referred object. However since reference classes are rarely sub-classed, @type is generally not useful in reference objects.

The @schemaLocation property can be used in resources to allow specifying user-defined properties of an Entity or to specify the expected characteristics of an entity.

The @baseType attribute gives a way to provide explicitly the base of class of a given resource that has been extended.

## RESOURCE MODEL

### Managed Entity and Task Resource Models

### SalesLead resource

A Sales Lead is a record that captures the initial interest expressed by a prospect (an individual or organization) in products or services. As a preliminary artifact in the sales funnel, it contains unverified information that must be nurtured and qualified. A lead is ultimately converted into a Sales Opportunity or is disqualified.

## Field descriptions

## SalesLead fields

| agreement | An AgreementRef \[0..\*\]. Array of references to agreementsor terms discussed with the prospect as part of this SalesLead. |
| --- | --- |
| category | A CategoryRef. Reference to a category in the catalog. |
| channel | A ChannelRef. The channel to which the resourcereference to. e.g. channel for selling product offerings,channel for opening a trouble ticket etc.. |
| creationDate | A DateTime. Date and time of the salesLead creation. |

![](data:image/png;base64,)

| description | A String. Concise and comprehensive description of theSales Lead. |
| --- | --- |
| href | A String. Hyperlink reference. |
| id | A String. Unique identifier. |
| lastUpdate | A DateTime. Date and time of the last update to the salesLead. |
| marketingCampaign | A MarketingCampaignRef. MarketingCampaign reference.Marketing campaign represents the carrier-initiatedmarketing activity which aims at the better recognitionabout its brand and offerings by the market. |
| marketSegment | A MarketSegmentRef. Provides references to thecorresponding market segment as target of productofferings. A market segment is grouping of Parties,GeographicAreas, SalesChannels, and so forth. |
| name | A String \[1\]. Name of the salesLead. |
| note | A Note \[0..\*\]. A user-generated text entry providingcontextual information or commentary. |
| priority | A SalesPriorityType. Urgency of working for this sales leador sales opportunity. ENUMERATED with values:\* low\* medium\* high |
| product | A ProductRef \[0..\*\]. Reference to the product(s) from theinventory associated with this Sales Lead. |
| productOffering | A ProductOfferingRef \[0..\*\]. List of product offerings thatthe prospect has shown interest in or that have beenproposed as part of this Sales Lead. |
| productSpecification | A ProductSpecificationRef \[0..\*\]. List of productspecifications related to the Sales Lead, defining thetechnical and/or functional characteristics of productsthat could be offered. |

![](data:image/png;base64,)

| prospectContactMedium | A ContactMedium \[0..\*\]. List of contact mediums for theprospect, including telephone, email, postal address, orother communication channels through which theprospect can be contacted.ContactMedium can be instantiated as\* EmailContactMedium\* FaxContactMedium\* GeographicAddressContactMedium\* PhoneContactMedium\* SocialContactMedium |
| --- | --- |
| rating | A String. Identifies the potential of a salesLead forbecoming a sale. Usual ratings for qualified leads are: hot,warm, cold. |
| referredDate | A DateTime. Date when the prospect information wasreceived (for example, from a trade show). |
| relatedParty | A RelatedPartyRefOrPartyRoleRef \[0..\*\]. List of relatedparties or party roles references associated with thisSales Lead, such as the prospect company, decision-makers, sales or marketing representatives, or otherstakeholders involved in the sales process. |
| revenueEstimate | A RevenueEstimate \[0..\*\]. Estimation of the revenue if thesalesLead turns into a sale. |
| salesLeadType | A String. Indicates the nature of the salesLead, such us:newBusiness, upsell, renewal, cross-sell, etc. |
| salesOpportunity | A SalesOpportunityRef \[0..\*\]. Reference to the salesopportunity that was created from this Sales Lead once itwas qualified and progressed through the sales process. |
| status | A SalesLeadStateType. Valid values for the lifecycle stateof a salesLead resource. ENUMERATED with values:\* accepted\* acknowledged\* cancelled\* inProgress\* pending\* rejected |
| statusChangeDate | A DateTime. Date and time of the last update of thestatus. |

![](data:image/png;base64,)

| statusChangeReason | A String. Reason why the status has changed. |
| --- | --- |
| validFor | A TimePeriod. A period of time, either as a deadline(endDateTime only) a startDateTime only, or both. |
| @baseType | A String. When sub-classing, this defines the super-class. |
| @schemaLocation | A String. A URI to a JSON-Schema file that definesadditional attributes and relationships. |
| @type | A String \[1\]. When sub-classing, this defines the sub-classExtensible name. |

**AgreementRef sub-resource fields**

Agreement reference. An agreement represents a contract or arrangement, either written or verbal and sometimes enforceable by law, such as a service level agreement or a customer price agreement. An agreement involves a number of other business entities, such as products, services, and resources and/or their specifications.

### SalesOpportunity resource

A Sales Opportunity represents a qualified potential for a sale, created when a prospect demonstrates a concrete and actionable interest. As a formal entry in the sales pipeline, it is tracked with an estimated value, a timeline, and a probability of success. Its lifecycle is managed through defined sales stages until it is won or lost.

# _Figure 3 - SalesOpportunity_

# Field descriptions

# SalesOpportunity fields

| agreement | An AgreementRef \[0..\*\]. A formal agreement thatdocuments the commercial terms and commitmentsnegotiated and agreed upon during the lifecycle of a salesopportunity. |
| --- | --- |
| category | A CategoryRef. Reference to a category in the catalog. |
| channel | A ChannelRef. The channel to which the resourcereference to. e.g. channel for selling product offerings,channel for opening a trouble ticket etc.. |
| creationDate | A DateTime. Date and time of the SalesOpportunitycreation. |

![](data:image/png;base64,)

| description | A String. Concise and comprehensive description of theSalesOpportunity. |
| --- | --- |
| href | A String. Hyperlink reference. |
| id | A String. Unique identifier. |
| marketingCampaign | A MarketingCampaignRef. MarketingCampaign reference.Marketing campaign represents the carrier-initiatedmarketing activity which aims at the better recognitionabout its brand and offerings by the market. |
| marketSegment | A MarketSegmentRef. Provides references to thecorresponding market segment as target of productofferings. A market segment is grouping of Parties,GeographicAreas, SalesChannels, and so forth. |
| name | A String \[1\]. Name of the SalesOpportunity. |
| note | A Note \[0..\*\]. A user-generated text entry providingcontextual information or commentary. |
| priority | A SalesPriorityType. Urgency of working for this sales leador sales opportunity. ENUMERATED with values:\* low\* medium\* high |
| quote | A QuoteRef \[0..\*\]. A formal offer, generated during thesales opportunity lifecycle, that details the proposedproducts, services, and pricing. |
| rating | A String. Identifies the potential of the opportunity forbecoming a sale, with common values being hot, warm, orcold. This overall rating is typically aggregated from itsitems, often reflecting the highest potential among them. |
| referredDate | A DateTime. Date when the prospect information wasreceived (for example, from a trade show). |
| relatedParty | A RelatedPartyRefOrPartyRoleRef \[0..\*\]. A reference to aninvolved party, which is identified either by its core entityor by the specific role it plays in the context of theinteraction. |

![](data:image/png;base64,)

| revenueEstimate | A RevenueEstimate \[0..\*\]. The aggregated andconsolidated total value of the revenue estimate for thesales opportunity, which can be derived from the sum ofits items or from a specific estimation at the opportunitylevel. |
| --- | --- |
| salesLead | A SalesLeadRef \[0..\*\]. References to the SalesLeadresources that gave rise to this SalesOpportunity. |
| salesOpportunityItem | A SalesOpportunityItem \[0..\*\]. A collection of line itemsthat constitutes the detailed scope of the salesopportunity, with each item specifying a target product orservice, its quantity, its estimated value and all specificinformation. |
| salesOpportunityType | A String. Indicates the nature of the SalesOpportunity,such us: newBusiness, upsell, renewal, cross-sell, etc. |
| salesProject | A SalesProjectRef \[0..\*\]. An array of references to salesprojects or initiatives to which this opportunity belongs. |
| status | A SalesOpportunityStateType. Valid values for thelifecycle state of a opportunity resource. ENUMERATEDwith values:\* accepted\* acknowledged\* cancelled\* inProgress\* pending\* rejected |
| statusChangeDate | A DateTime. Date and time of the last update of status. |
| statusChangeReason | A String. Reason why the status has changed. |
| validFor | A TimePeriod. A period of time, either as a deadline(endDateTime only) a startDateTime only, or both. |
| @baseType | A String. When sub-classing, this defines the super-class. |
| @schemaLocation | A String. A URI to a JSON-Schema file that definesadditional attributes and relationships. |

**AgreementRef sub-resource fields**

![](data:image/png;base64,)

Agreement reference. An agreement represents a contract or arrangement, either written or verbal and sometimes enforceable by law, such as a service level agreement or a customer price agreement. An agreement involves a number of other business entities, such as products, services, and resources and/or their specifications.

See \[AgreementRef\] for details.

**CategoryRef sub-resource fields**

Reference to a category in the catalog.

See \[CategoryRef\] for details.

**ChannelRef sub-resource fields**

The channel to which the resource reference to. e.g. channel for selling product offerings, channel for opening a trouble ticket etc..

See \[ChannelRef\] for details.

**MarketingCampaignRef sub-resource fields**

MarketingCampaign reference. Marketing campaign represents the carrier-initiated marketing activity which aims at the better recognition about its brand and offerings by the market.

See \[MarketingCampaignRef\] for details.

**MarketSegmentRef sub-resource fields**

Provides references to the corresponding market segment as target of product offerings. A market segment is grouping of Parties, GeographicAreas, SalesChannels, and so forth.

See \[MarketSegmentRef\] for details.

Extra information about a given entity.

## Notification Resource Models

8 notifications are defined for this API.

Notifications related to SalesLead:

- Create Event
- Delete Event
- Attribute Value Change Event
- State Change Event

Notifications related to SalesOpportunity:

- Create Event
- Delete Event
- Attribute Value Change Event
- State Change Event

The notification structure for all notifications in this API follow the pattern depicted by the figure below. A notification event resource (depicted by "SpecificEvent" placeholder) is a sub class of a generic Event structure containing at least an id of the event occurrence (eventId), an event timestamp (eventTime), and the name of the resource (eventType). This notification structure owns an event payload structure ("SpecificEventPayload" placeholder) linked to the resource concerned by the notification using the resource name as access field ("resourceName" placeholder).

![](data:image/png;base64,)

![](data:image/png;base64,)

# API OPERATIONS

Remember the following Uniform Contract:

| **Operation on Entities** | **Uniform API Operation** | **Description** |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Query Entities | GET Resource | GET must be used to retrievea representation of aresource. |
| Create Entity | POST Resource | POST must be used to createa new resource |
| Partial Update of an Entity | PATCH Resource | PATCH must be used topartially update a resource |
| Remove an Entity | DELETE Resource | DELETE must be used toremove a resource |
| Execute an Action on anEntity | POST on TASK Resource | POST must be used toexecute Task Resources |
| Other Request Methods | POST on TASK Resource | GET and POST must not beused to tunnel other requestmethods. |

Filtering and attribute selection rules are described in the TMF REST Design Guidelines.

Notifications are also described in a subsequent section.

## Operations on SalesLead

### Retrieves a salesLead by ID

```
GET /salesLead/{id}?fields=…
```

**Description**

### Updates partially a salesLead

```
PATCH /salesLead/{id}?fields=…
```

**Description**

This operation allows partial updates of a SalesLead entity. Support of json/merge ([https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc7396)](https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc7396) is mandatory, support of json/patch ([http://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc5789)](http://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc5789) is optional. Note: If the update operation yields to the creation of sub-resources or relationships, the same rules concerning mandatory sub- resource attributes and default value settings in the POST operation applies to the PATCH operation. Hence these tables are not repeated here.

**Patchable and Non Patchable Attributes**

| **Non Patchable Attributes** | **Rule** |
| --- | --- |
| creationDate |  |
| href |  |
| id |  |
| @baseType | @baseType is immutable |
| @schemaLocation | @schemaLocation is immutable |
| @type | @type is immutable |

| agreement |  |

| lastUpdate |  |

### Updates partially a salesOpportunity

### PATCH /salesOpportunity/{id}?fields=…

### Description

![](data:image/png;base64,)

This operation allows partial updates of a SalesOpportunity entity. Support of json/merge ([https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc7396)](https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc7396) is mandatory, support of json/patch ([http://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc5789)](http://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc5789) is optional. Note: If the update operation yields to the creation of sub-resources or relationships, the same rules concerning mandatory sub- resource attributes and default value settings in the POST operation applies to the PATCH operation. Hence these tables are not repeated here.

**Patchable and Non Patchable Attributes**

| **Non Patchable Attributes** | **Rule** |
| --- | --- |
| creationDate |  |
| href |  |
| id |  |
| @baseType | @baseType is immutable |
| @schemaLocation | @schemaLocation is immutable |
| @type | @type is immutable |

| **Patchable Attributes** | **Rule** |
| --- | --- |
| agreement |  |
| category |  |
| channel |  |
| description |  |
| marketingCampaign |  |
| marketSegment |  |
| name |  |
| note |  |
| priority |  |
| quote |  |
| rating |  |
| referredDate |  |
| relatedParty |  |
| revenueEstimate |  |
| salesLead |  |

![](data:image/png;base64,)

| **Patchable Attributes** | **Rule** |
| --- | --- |
| salesOpportunityItem |  |
| salesOpportunityType |  |
| salesProject |  |
| status |  |
| statusChangeDate |  |
| statusChangeReason |  |
| validFor |  |

```
DELETE /salesOpportunity/{id}?{filtering}
```

**Description**

This operation deletes a SalesOpportunity entity.

**Usage samples**

**Request**

```
DELETE /salesOpportunity/7894325Content-Type: application/json
```

204

# API NOTIFICATIONS

For every single of operation on the entities use the following templates and provide sample REST notification POST calls.

It is assumed that the Pub/Sub uses the Register and UnRegister mechanisms described in the REST Guidelines reproduced below.

## Register listener

**POST /hub**

**Description**

Sets the communication endpoint address the service instance must use to deliver information about its health state, execution state, failures and metrics. Subsequent POST calls will be rejected by the service if it does not support multiple listeners. In this case DELETE /api/hub/{id} must be called before an endpoint can be created again.

**Behavior**

Returns HTTP/1.1 status code 204 if the request was successful.

Returns HTTP/1.1 status code 409 if request is not successful.

**Usage Samples**

Here’s an example of a request for registering a listener.

**Request**

```
POST /api/hub
Accept: application/json
{
    "callback": "http://in.listener.com"
}
```

**Response**

```
Content-Type: application/json
Location: /api/hub/42
```

![](data:image/png;base64,)

```
{
    "id":"42",
    "callback": "http://in.listener.com",    "query":""
}
```

## Unregister listener

**DELETE /hub/{id}**

**Description**

Clears the communication endpoint address that was set by creating the Hub..

**Behavior**

Returns HTTP/1.1 status code 204 if the request was successful.

Returns HTTP/1.1 status code 404 if the resource is not found.

**Usage Samples**

Here’s an example of a request for un-registering a listener.

**Request**

```
DELETE /api/hub/42
Accept: application/json
```

**Response**

## Publish Event to listener

**POST /client/listener**

**Description**

Clears the communication endpoint address that was set by creating the Hub.

Provides to a registered listener the description of the event that was raised. The /client/listener url is the callback url passed when registering the listener.

![](data:image/png;base64,)

**Behavior**

Returns HTTP/1.1 status code 201 if the service is able to set the configuration.

**Usage Samples**

Here’s an example of a notification received by the listener. In this example “EVENT TYPE” should be replaced by one of the notification types supported by this API (see Notification resources Models section) and EVENT BODY refers to the data structure of the given notification type.

**Request**

```
POST /client/listener
Accept: application/json
{
    "event": {
        EVENT BODY    },
    "eventType": "EVENT_TYPE"}
```

**Response**

```
201
```

For detailed examples on the general TM Forum notification mechanism, see the TMF REST Design Guidelines.
